explanation: For each of the first k positions, uniformly choose one still-unselected entry and swap it into place. This partial Fisher–Yates shuffle preserves the full multiset and makes every k-element subset equally likely.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: At position i, every still-unselected entry has equal chance of being chosen from the remaining suffix. Thus every ordered k-tuple of distinct entries has probability 1/(n·(n−1)···(n−k+1)), and summing over its k! orders makes every k-element subset equally likely. Swaps preserve the full multiset.
walkthrough: For k=2 and [4,7,9], one possible pair of draws chooses 9 first and 4 second, leaving sample prefix [9,4]. The possible subsets {4,7}, {4,9} and {7,9} each have probability 1/3.
edgeCases: k equal to the length chooses all entries.
Entries outside the sampled prefix remain part of the preserved full multiset.
